speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; have you noticed any specific patterns to the rash or any joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).

The clinical picture of a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities appearing one week after low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache, combined with a distinctive facial rash that spares the perioral area, is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection.
